title: Fourth Word Comparison On The Necessity Of The Prescribed Prayers

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the comparison in this passage?
questions.answer: The lesson is that the daily prayers are very valuable, easy to gain, and foolish to neglect.

questions.question: How many gold pieces did the ruler give to each servant?
questions.answer: He gave each servant twenty-four gold pieces.

questions.question: Where did the ruler send the two servants?
questions.answer: He sent them to live on one of his rich farms.

questions.question: How far away was that place?
questions.answer: It was two months away.

questions.question: What did the ruler tell them to use the money for?
questions.answer: He told them to use it for tickets and for things needed for their home there.

questions.question: What kinds of travel were available on the way?
questions.answer: There were road vehicles, trains, boats, and airplanes.

questions.question: What did the wise servant do with some of his money before reaching the station?
questions.answer: He spent a small part of it in a useful way that brought great profit and pleased his master.

questions.question: What happened to his money because of that good use?
questions.answer: It grew many times over.

questions.question: What did the careless servant do with most of his money?
questions.answer: He wasted it on gambling and entertainment.

questions.question: How much money did he have left after wasting the rest?
questions.answer: He had one gold piece left.

questions.question: What did his friend advise him to do with the last coin?
questions.answer: He told him to buy a ticket with it.

questions.question: Why was buying the ticket so important?
questions.answer: It would keep him from making the long trip on foot and from going hungry.

questions.question: What hope did the friend give about the master?
questions.answer: He said the master might forgive him and even let him ride on an airplane.

questions.question: If the servant refused to buy the ticket, what hard thing would happen to him?
questions.answer: He would have to cross a desert alone and hungry for two months.

questions.question: What does the passage show about spending a little for something important?
questions.answer: It shows that using a small amount for a great benefit is wise.

questions.question: What statement at the beginning tells us how important prayer is in religion?
questions.answer: It says that the prescribed prayers hold religion up like a pillar supports a building.

questions.question: What kind of story is used to explain this lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison story is used.

questions.question: Who are the main people in the story?
questions.answer: A powerful ruler and two servants are the main people.

questions.question: What was the servants’ mission?
questions.answer: They were to travel and settle in the ruler’s rich property far away.

questions.question: What stop was one day away from the farm?
questions.answer: A station was one day away from it.

questions.question: Which servant acted in a smart and successful way?
questions.answer: The fortunate servant did.

questions.question: What shows that he was careful with his money?
questions.answer: He used only a little on the way and spent it in a beneficial way.

questions.question: Which servant acted in a lazy and wasteful way?
questions.answer: The unlucky servant did.

questions.question: What do gambling and amusements show about his choices?
questions.answer: They show that he cared more about fun than about his real goal.

questions.question: What did the friend compare the ticket to?
questions.answer: He compared it to a key that opens a treasure.

questions.question: What does that comparison help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that a small cost can open the way to a huge reward.

questions.question: Why would it be stubborn to refuse to buy the ticket?
questions.answer: Because the servant still had enough to get help for the journey but chose passing pleasure instead.

questions.question: What can we infer about the ruler from the friend’s words?
questions.answer: The ruler is generous and willing to show mercy.

questions.question: What words in the passage show the judgment about neglecting this chance?
questions.answer: It is described as foolish, harmful, and senseless.

questions.question: What overall choice does the story tell readers to make?
questions.answer: It tells readers to choose the small cost that leads to great good instead of short-lived enjoyment.

questions.question: Why does the passage say to pay attention to the story?
questions.answer: Because it helps explain clearly how precious prayer is and how wrong it is to ignore it.

questions.question: What level of certainty does the passage use to show this lesson is very clear?
questions.answer: It says it is as clear as a simple math fact.

questions.question: What was special about the ruler’s farm?
questions.answer: It was rich and royal.

questions.question: What two things were the servants told to prepare for with their money?
questions.answer: They were told to prepare for travel and for setting up their home there.

questions.question: Why is the station important in the story?
questions.answer: It is the point from which they could continue the journey more easily.

questions.question: How did the first servant’s spending differ from the second servant’s spending?
questions.answer: The first spent a little wisely, while the second spent almost everything foolishly.

questions.question: What result came from the first servant’s wise action?
questions.answer: His money increased greatly and his master was pleased.

questions.question: What result came from the second servant’s foolish action?
questions.answer: He was left almost empty-handed and faced a very hard trip.

questions.question: What does the friend’s advice tell us about true wisdom?
questions.answer: True wisdom is to use what remains for what is necessary, not for extra pleasure.

questions.question: What problem would the servant face besides hunger if he did not buy the ticket?
questions.answer: He would have to travel by himself across a desert.

questions.question: Why does the story mention different ways of travel like trains and airplanes?
questions.answer: It shows that there were easier ways available if the servants used their money properly.

questions.question: What does the desert in the story suggest about the journey without the ticket?
questions.answer: It suggests hardship, danger, and difficulty.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast short pleasure with long-term benefit?
questions.answer: It shows that quick fun can destroy a person’s chance for something much better later.

questions.question: What can a reader conclude about self-control from this comparison?
questions.answer: Self-control helps a person save for what truly matters.

questions.question: What is one strong reason the careless servant’s choice is called harmful?
questions.answer: His choice made his future much harder just for a little temporary fun.

questions.question: What religious act is the passage teaching about?
questions.answer: It is teaching about the prescribed daily prayers.

questions.question: According to the opening line, what role do these prayers have in religion?
questions.answer: They are a main support of religion.

questions.question: What did the ruler give equally to both servants?
questions.answer: He gave both the same amount of money.

questions.question: What does this equal gift show about the start of their journey?
questions.answer: It shows they both began with the same opportunity.

questions.question: What choice made the difference between the two servants?
questions.answer: The difference came from how they used their money.

questions.question: What kind of person is the successful servant shown to be?
questions.answer: He is careful, wise, and goal-focused.

questions.question: What kind of person is the unsuccessful servant shown to be?
questions.answer: He is careless, lazy, and driven by amusement.

questions.question: Why did the successful servant’s spending please the master?
questions.answer: Because he used it in a way that brought great benefit.

questions.question: What does the friend want to protect the careless servant from?
questions.answer: He wants to protect him from a long, hungry, lonely journey.

questions.question: What does the possibility of riding on an airplane add to the advice?
questions.answer: It adds hope that things could become much easier if he made the right choice.

questions.question: What does the story suggest about using the last chance wisely?
questions.answer: It suggests that even one small chance should not be wasted.

questions.question: Why is spending the last coin on wrongdoing presented as especially foolish?
questions.answer: Because that coin could save him from great hardship and lead to safety.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage want the reader to have about neglecting prayer?
questions.answer: It wants the reader to feel that neglecting prayer is a serious mistake.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage want the reader to have about prayer itself?
questions.answer: It wants the reader to see prayer as precious and worth the effort.

questions.question: Write the message of the story in one sentence.
questions.answer: A small, wise effort for prayer brings great benefit, but wasting that chance brings loss.

questions.question: What is being compared in this passage to help the reader understand prayer?
questions.answer: A journey with money, tickets, and two servants is used to explain prayer.

questions.question: Why did the ruler send the servants out instead of leaving them where they were?
questions.answer: He wanted them to travel and settle in a better place prepared for them.

questions.question: What does the ruler’s command show about his planning?
questions.answer: It shows that he had already provided a way for them to reach their destination.

questions.question: How did the fortunate servant treat the ruler’s gift?
questions.answer: He treated it responsibly and used part of it for good benefit.

questions.question: How did the other servant treat the ruler’s gift?
questions.answer: He treated it carelessly and wasted almost all of it.

questions.question: What does the huge increase in the first servant’s money show?
questions.answer: It shows that wise spending can bring great reward.

questions.question: What does the loss of almost all the second servant’s money show?
questions.answer: It shows that sinful or foolish choices can leave a person weak and unprepared.

questions.question: What warning does the friend give about not buying the ticket?
questions.answer: He warns that the servant will face a difficult trip on foot with hunger and loneliness.

questions.question: Why is the ticket described like something that opens a treasure?
questions.answer: Because it gives access to something much greater than its own small price.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about pleasure that only lasts a short time?
questions.answer: It teaches that short pleasure is not worth losing a great future benefit.

questions.question: If someone only cared about immediate fun, which servant would he resemble?
questions.answer: He would resemble the careless servant.

questions.question: If someone thinks ahead and prepares for what matters most, which servant would he resemble?
questions.answer: He would resemble the fortunate servant.

questions.question: What can we infer about the journey if proper transport is used?
questions.answer: It becomes much easier and faster.

questions.question: What can we infer about the journey if a person refuses proper help?
questions.answer: It becomes exhausting and miserable.

questions.question: How does this comparison encourage students to think about salah?
questions.answer: It encourages them to see salah as a small effort that leads to a huge good.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the cost of gaining the value of prayer?
questions.answer: It says the cost is very small.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person who neglects prayer?
questions.answer: It says that person is acting in a very foolish and harmful way.

questions.question: What did both servants receive before beginning the journey?
questions.answer: They each received twenty-four gold pieces and instructions.

questions.question: What were they expected to do at the end of the journey?
questions.answer: They were expected to settle in the ruler’s rich place.

questions.question: What opportunity did the first servant make good use of on the road?
questions.answer: He used part of his money in a profitable way before reaching the station.

questions.question: How did that choice affect his relationship with the master?
questions.answer: It pleased the master.

questions.question: What poor habits are named for the second servant?
questions.answer: Gambling, entertainment, laziness, and stubbornness are named.

questions.question: Why does his friend speak to him so directly?
questions.answer: Because the servant is in danger of making an obviously bad choice.

questions.question: What is the benefit of spending the final coin the right way?
questions.answer: It can secure the trip and possibly bring even more help.

questions.question: What mistake would the servant make if he used the last coin for sinful fun?
questions.answer: He would trade a major need for a tiny and passing pleasure.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the desert add to the story?
questions.answer: It shows how severe the hardship would be without the ticket.

questions.question: What thinking skill does the passage ask the reader to use when judging the servant’s choice?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to use clear reasoning and common sense.

questions.question: Why is the bad servant called not only foolish but also harmful?
questions.answer: Because his choice hurts his own future and brings suffering on himself.

questions.question: What good character quality is shown by the first servant?
questions.answer: He shows responsibility.

questions.question: What is one big message a Muslim student can learn from this passage?
questions.answer: A wise Muslim should not waste what Allah gives, but should use it for what truly benefits him.
